subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & third-party subprocessors (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Halpern <sarah.halpern@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-discovery)

Hi Sarah 	6

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the data/privacy items you flagged: 

Summary from our call:
- Data residency: FinTechCo requires US-only processing.
- PII: incoming customer PII will be sent in prompts; you asked for options to avoid storing raw PII and for tokenization/redaction controls.
- Retention & logging: you requested short retention for request/response logs (you mentioned ~30 days) and strict controls on any telemetry.
- Third-party subprocessors: you want to restrict telemetry vendors; cloud provider (AWS) is acceptable pending controls. Marketplace flows (3rd-party connectors) need review.

Attachments included: redwood-subprocessors-2026.pdf (current subprocessor list) and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) to align on milestones. I've also linked our SOC2 report in the MAP.

Quick answers / options we can offer now:
- Data residency: We can pin the tenant to US-only regions (AWS us-east-1) for both hosted and Dedicated deployments.
- PII handling: Options: 1) customer-side tokenization before sending requests; 2) runtime redaction rules; 3) dedicated Private deployment so data never leaves your VPC. We can walk through tradeoffs 	tokenization offers the best low-friction integration but requires client changes.
- Retention/logging: We can set logs retention to 30 days and disable detailed telemetry exports. Audit logs and admin traces can be retained longer under your control if needed.
- Subprocessors: Our standard list is attached. For FinTechCo we can remove telemetry vendors (e.g., Datadog/Sentry) from your tenant and limit to AWS + Splunk (if Splunk is required) via contractual commitments.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm: (a) US-only processing? (b) 30-day logs retention acceptable? (c) Any allowed telemetry vendors we should preserve (e.g., Splunk)?
2) If yes, we'll prepare an updated MAP + security addendum and loop in legal (Aisha).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical follow-up with Dev to confirm deployment model and tokenization options 	 propose Tue 12/8 or Wed 12/9.

Would you like us to prepare the security addendum and redlineable contract with those constraints, or do you want to take a first pass?

Thanks 	talk soon.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2026.pdf, mutual-action-plan-FT-2026-479.xlsx

From: Sarah Halpern <sarah.halpern@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-discovery)

Hi Marissa 	6

Thanks for the clear summary 	6 very helpful. Confirmations and a few clarifications from our InfoSec/procurement side: 

1) Data residency: Confirmed 	6 processing must be US-only.
2) Retention: We require logs and request/response artifacts to be retained no longer than 30 days by default. We may request longer retention for specific audit windows, but that will be by exception.
3) PII: We prefer customer-side tokenization where feasible. If not possible, runtime redaction is acceptable provided we have verifiable proofs and config controls (field-level redaction rules).
4) Subprocessors: Our policy allows cloud providers (AWS) and our SIEM (Splunk Cloud). We do NOT allow general telemetry vendors (Datadog, Sentry) to receive request/response payloads or logs containing PII.
5) Marketplace flows: Any third-party connector that sends data outside of the pinned AWS region must be disabled. We need a clear list of marketplace integrations and the ability to opt-out per-tenant.

Procurement would like a security addendum + subprocessor attestation and SOC2 report before contract signature. Can you supply:
- Up-to-date subprocessor list (CSV/PDF)
- SOC2 report (redacted allowed)
- An explicit statement that telemetry to third parties can be disabled for our tenant

We can do Tue 12/8 at 10:30am PT for the technical follow-up with Dev. If that works, please send a calendar invite.

Thanks 	6
Sarah Halpern
Head of Security & Compliance, FinTechCo
sarah.halpern@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Halpern <sarah.halpern@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-discovery)

Hi Sarah 	6

Appreciate the clear guidance. We can comply with the constraints you listed. Specifics: 

- US-only: we will pin your tenant to AWS us-east-1 and prevent cross-region failover unless explicitly requested and contractually approved.
- Retention: we will configure request/response logs to 30 days for your tenant. Admin audit logs can be retained longer under your control; we'll note that in the addendum.
- PII/tokenization: Dev has implemented runtime redaction rules; we can also support tokenization helpers in our client libs. We'll include sample code and a migration checklist in the MAP.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessor PDF (redwood-subprocessors-2026.pdf). For FinTechCo we will: 1) exclude Datadog/Sentry from your tenant telemetry; 2) limit outbound telemetry to AWS services and Splunk Cloud (if you confirm Splunk). We will add a contractual clause guaranteeing telemetry disablement for your tenant.
- Marketplace connectors: We will provide a list of marketplace integrations and a per-tenant opt-out switch.

Next steps I'll action this week:
- Send updated MAP + security addendum (including subprocessor attestation).
- Attach SOC2 report and produce the redlineable contract.
- Dev will join the Tue 12/8 10:30am PT call to walk deployment/tokenization options.

Aisha (legal)  looping you in to prepare the addendum and confirm we can insert the telemetry-disable clause and the subprocessor opt-out language.

Marissa

Attachments: SOC2-report-2026.pdf, redwood-subprocessors-2026.pdf
